[anomalyco/opencode#47675](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47675)
 doesn't move Auto server-side. It revives the permission.ask plugin hook, which happens to run inside Permission.ask before pending.set and before Event.Asked is published — so a plugin verdict resolves the request without ever emitting a user-attention event. Built-in Auto is untouched, so on its own it doesn't fix your case.

Where they meet: both touch packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts and packages/core/src/v1/permission.ts, so they will conflict. Mine is small (+412/-7) and ready; yours is the larger change with an open design question. Happy to rebase onto yours whenever it lands — no need to sequence around me.

One thing the lease model may need to settle: with the hook alive, a plugin can answer ask on a request Auto would have covered. Does the lease win, or the plugin? Failing toward the prompt looks right to me, but it is worth being explicit — otherwise the "resolved before the event" property you are adding can be undone by a plugin, and the notifications come back intermittently.

@Rocklis Ran the batch you asked for. Short version: **no measurable difference in premature stops, because at
this scale the failure mode didn't occur in either build** — but the change is behaviourally live and
shows no regression. Details:

**Setup.** Two `git worktree`s at `5cf9f51` (your base) and `5de5c9a` (PR head), diff confirmed to be
only the 4 files in the PR. Run from source with bun 1.4.0:
`bun run --cwd packages/opencode src/index.ts run --pure --auto --format json --dir <fresh temp dir> -m <provider>/<model>`,
prompt piped on stdin. Model is `gpt-5.5` behind a LiteLLM gateway registered as a custom provider with
`npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"` — the exact path your ternary gates on. `--pure` (verified: no external
plugin loaded), per-arm `HOME`/XDG dirs, a fresh empty working directory per run, no session reuse.

One deliberate config deviation you should know about: I stripped `skills.paths` and `plugin` from my
normal config. A pilot showed the local skill library dominated the system prompt and provoked `skill`
tool calls that had nothing to do with what we're measuring. The provider block, model, and `agent.*.steps`
are untouched, and both arms ran the identical trimmed config. If you'd rather see it with a large skill
library in the prompt, that's a different experiment and I'm happy to run it.

**Instrument check first.** Statically, `provider()` returns a 9274-char prompt containing
`## Response channels` on the base and a 7429-char prompt without it on the PR head. At runtime the
first-step input token counts separate cleanly — base 6167–6232 (n=80), PR head 5801–5829 for 79 of 80 runs
(one outlier at 9768, a run with an apparent provider retry).
So the arms genuinely differ in the intended way.

**Design.** 10 tasks (6 short multi-step, 4 long ones that explicitly require a progress update *before
each edit* and forbid batching), each with a machine-checkable filesystem criterion — no LLM judging.
8 reps per task per arm, arms interleaved back-to-back in randomized order per (task, rep) so gateway
drift cancels. Runs serialized. **160 runs total, 80 per arm.**

**Buckets.** A run is a *premature stop* if the last `step_finish` reason is `stop`, there were no tool
calls after the last `step_start` (text-only final turn), **and** the criterion is not met; a *normal
final answer* if the same shape but the criterion is met; *other* for errors, timeouts, non-`stop`
finishes.

**Result:**

| arm | premature stop | normal final answer | other | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `5cf9f51` | 0 | 80 | 0 | 80 |
| PR head `5de5c9a` | 0 | 80 | 0 | 80 |

Fisher exact p = 1.00, but with a 0-vs-0 table that's a formality. The meaningful bound: zero events in
80 runs puts the premature-stop rate at ≤ 3.7 % per arm (95 %, one-sided). All 160 runs completed their
task; the finish-reason split alone was `{stop: 80}` vs `{stop: 80}`.

**Why it didn't reproduce.** The traces explain it: this model emits its progress narration *in the same
assistant message as the tool call*, so the step finishes with reason `tool-calls` and the loop continues.
The bug needs a commentary message with **no** tool call. That never happened spontaneously here, even on
the tasks designed to force it.

**Classifier positive control.** To make sure the zeroes aren't an instrument failure, I ran a task that
instructs the model to stop mid-work with text only, scored against a criterion it cannot satisfy:
**8/8 runs (4 per arm) were correctly bucketed as premature stops**, with exactly the bug's trace shape
(`apply_patch` → `step_finish tool-calls` → text-only step → `step_finish stop`, run exits with work
outstanding). A bad-model-id run correctly landed in `other`. All three buckets fire.

**One thing that is a real signal.** Counting mid-task (non-final) assistant text parts, paired by
(task, rep): base > PR head in **33** pairs, PR head > base in **0**, **47** ties — exact sign test
p ≈ 1.2e-10, about +0.44 extra narration turns per run on

@Rocklis Ran the batch you asked for and posted the full write-up on #47355 (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47355#issuecomment-5573081645), since it bears on the merge decision.

Headline for anyone following the issue: **160 paired runs, 80 per arm, zero premature stops in either build.** That is a null from non-occurrence, not evidence of no effect — the failure mode needs a commentary message with *no* accompanying tool call, and `gpt-5.5` on the openai-compatible path emits its narration inside the same message as the tool call, so the step finishes `tool-calls` and the loop continues. A forced positive control (8/8) confirms the classifier fires, so the zeroes are a real absence rather than a dead instrument.

What the batch does show is that the prompt change is behaviourally live in the intended direction: mid-task narration turns drop on the PR head in 33 of 80 pairs and rise in 0 (sign test p ≈ 1.2e-10).

So the original report stands unexplained at the rate level. My own observation came from long interactive sessions rather than the short scripted tasks used here, and 80 runs per arm only bounds the rate at ≤3.7% — too coarse to see something that surfaces over a long session. Leaving this issue open on that basis rather than treating the batch as a resolution.

Repro on opencode v1.18.29, Linux, same silent drop at depth 2.

Chain: orchestrator (depth 0) -> task oracle (depth 1) -> task scout (depth 2). Scout runs a chained command containing `cat /GLOSSARY.md` (root file). Tree-sitter splits the chain, scan.dirs aggregates to `/`, external_directory `/*` evaluates to ask. No answerable prompt in the session UI (an OS notification may fire via the TUI notifications plugin, but there is no prompt to act on); bash stays running until manual abort:

- 3 scout sessions stuck ~40/~39/~17 min (one exemplar: `ses_f86e4958cffeoHyZ0Uq3STM3hJ`; full session IDs and row dumps available on request)

Steps: 1. depth-2 subagent 2. chained bash touching `/` 3. external_directory ask fires 4. parent shows no prompt, tool pends, only abort recovers.

Depth 0 and depth 1 ASKs surface correctly (verified live same day, accepted and resolved). Chained-command matching is aggregated (shell.ts collect); external_directory is evaluated before bash matching.

Code reading (dev@57ef382843, not ground truth): two paths drop the ASK. TUI: routes/session/index.tsx:206-211+232-235 — children() only aggregates direct children of the viewed session, so a depth-2 ASK is never rendered (and permissions() returns [] when viewing a child session). CLI run: run.ts:801-821 — if (!sessions.has(sessionID)) continue drops the event for an untracked child, so the Deferred at permission/index.ts:98-102 never resolves.

#35073 (fix subagent permission hang) closed 2026-09-04, ~17h before the 1.18.29 install — our 06-07 Sept repro proves the depth-2 drop survives that fix. Searched permission ask subagent — #44747 is the survivor of the permission bucket (bot duplicate pointed at now-closed #35073/#36868).

Independent corpus confirming this for pre-default binaries, plus one hang surviving the default — opencode v1.18.29, Linux, openai-compatible gateway (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash), code dev@57ef382843.

Corrected mining (aborts excluded): 341 assistant messages with empty finish → ~308 ordinary aborts (MessageAbortedError + time.completed set) to exclude + 11 fast aborts with completed present to distinguish → 22-33 true hangs by strictness (finish NULL + error NULL, never completed). In-flight message excluded — same DB signature as a hang.

31/33 sampled hangs (94%) are on binaries 1.1.49→1.18.27 without default (before 04 Sept 19:26) — matches the reported bug. But one authentic hang 2026-09-07 11:57 occurred under 1.18.29 with the ?? 300_000 default active (provider.ts:1795-1796, literal present in installed binary): ses_f845f8ac, delta 2ms, time.completed NULL. The default does not eliminate all hangs.

Two shapes, part rows confirm chunk-by-chunk persistence:
- zero-byte: 0 parts, lifetime <1s. ex msg_0795edebc0011V1CkxmazEnIwu, 28ms.
- stall after start: ex msg_07943d23d001CJcskVN90yYPpn, 108s of reasoning persisted, then silence.

Provider was reachable: parallel stream on same API/model succeeded at the same second (logs 00:57Z). Zero timeout / retry / ECONNRESET lines in hang windows; only the later manual cancel + Aborted.

Code lead (dev@57ef382843, not ground truth): wrapSSE arms only if content-type contains "text/event-stream" (provider.ts:37-40) — a gateway answering otherwise (SSE-in-JSON, chunked) escapes the guard.

Workaround validated in prod:
`{ "provider": { "<id>": { "options": { "chunkTimeout": 120000 } } } }`

## Workaround found for stuck tool calls

The "tool call stuck in running" pattern has a root cause and a fix.

### Root cause

A bash script used `exec` to start a daemon:

```bash
exec /path/to/daemon.py
```

`exec` replaces the shell process with the daemon. Since opencode's bash tool waits for the command to complete, and the daemon runs forever, the bash tool hangs forever. The session becomes permanently stuck.

### Fix

Replace `exec` with background execution:

```bash
/path/to/daemon.py &
disown
sleep 1
```

This runs the daemon in the background and detaches it, so the bash tool exits cleanly.

### Verification

After applying this fix:
- The daemon starts successfully
- The bash tool completes without hanging
- The session continues to work normally
- No stuck tool calls

### Suggestion for opencode

Consider adding a timeout to bash tool execution, or detecting when a command uses `exec` and warning the user that it may cause the session to hang.

Reproduced the election flip and traced it to the catalog's availability predicate. The mechanism is a two-step chain, and it's narrower than "any config block promotes a provider":

**Step 1 — the config block inherits the upstream model catalog.** `provider.ts:1423-1434` (`mergeProvider`): a `provider.<id>` block from config is merged onto the matching `database[providerID]` entry (the models.dev-style catalog), so `{"anthropic": {"options": {"baseURL": ...}}}` arrives with anthropic's entire stock model list attached — the block didn't have to declare any models to get them.

**Step 2 — a credential-less, integration-less provider counts as "available".** `catalog.ts:71-77`: `available()` returns true when `provider.integrationID === undefined && !integration`. A config-sourced block with no `env`/auth and no plugin integration satisfies exactly that, so all those inherited models enter `model.available()`.

**Why the default flips to that specific model:** `catalog.ts:215-232` (`model.default()`) has no persisted default, so it sorts `model.available()` by `time.released` descending and takes the head. Claude Sonnet's release timestamp beats `gpt-5.3-chat-latest`'s, so adding the block elects the newest Anthropic catalog entry — and only then does the missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` surface at call time.

**On the suggested directions:** option 1 (options-only blocks don't elect) treats the symptom at the catalog layer, but note the repo already has a working precedent for "baseURL means configure, not elect" — the custom loaders at `provider.ts:736-738` and `774-775` (cloudflare-workers-ai / cloudflare-ai-gateway) return `{ autoload: false }` precisely when `options.baseURL` is set, i.e. "URL configured → don't treat this as activation". Extending that same semantic to the generic config-block path would be consistent with existing behavior. Option 2 (credential-ranked) would also change behavior for integration-based providers that legitimately have no static credential, so it's the broader blast radius of the two.

One more data point for whichever direction is picked: the failure is *silent at the config layer* — the user only sees the wrong-provider error at call time. If the coupling is kept intentionally (option 3), it would be worth a startup-level warning when a provider becomes "available" with zero credential sources (env, config env, auth, integration all empty), because that state is currently indistinguishable from a working setup until the first request fails.

Same symptom on **OpenCode Desktop 1.18.18 → 1.18.29** on Windows 10. Reproduces in fresh empty sessions and tiny windows. Below are reproducible measurements that add Desktop-specific data (renderer/GPU CPU burn per keystroke) and document the ruled-out causes.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

### Title
Desktop (Windows): composer keystroke lag with stop-and-go freezing — independent of session size, window size, and data size; renderer + GPU processes burn CPU on every keystroke

### Environment
- OpenCode Desktop **1.18.18** → updated to **1.18.29** (Sep 2026): **bug reproduces in both**
- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045 (build 19045)
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X (12C/24T), 64 GB RAM, NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB (driver 566.36, status OK), display 2560x1440
- Antivirus: Avast active (Defender passive) — ruled out, see below
- Data dir: `~/.local/share/opencode`

### Summary
Typing in the Desktop composer intermittently freezes: characters appear in bursts, with a repeating stop-and-go pattern (cursor advances, stalls ~200–300 ms, resumes). It is much worse while the agent streams/executes tools, but persists even with the app idle. It reproduces in a **brand-new empty session** and with the **window resized to a few pixels**, and still reproduces after pruning the database from 3 GB to 644 MB.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open OpenCode Desktop on Windows, any project.
2. Hold the spacebar (or type continuously) in the composer while the app is idle → input advances/stalls/resumes repeatedly.
3. Repeat while the agent is streaming a response → input delay worsens noticeably.
4. Repeat in a fresh empty session and with a very small window → identical behavior.

### What we measured (PowerShell sampling, 500 ms resolution, `Get-Process` CPU deltas)
Identified Electron roles via `Win32_Process.CommandLine`:

| Process (role) | Behavior while typing (app idle) |
|---|---|
| **renderer** | 30–90 ms CPU per 500 ms sample, continuously; periodic spikes of **200–300 ms** |
| **GPU process** | busy in lockstep with the renderer (compositing per keystroke) |
| **main (hosts the opencode server)** | mostly idle during typing |
| **Notepad** (held simultaneously, same period) | **0 ms** — control group |

- With the app fully idle (no typing): ~0 CPU and ~0 disk I/O across all processes.
- While the agent streams: the DB event table receives `message.updated.1` / `message.part.updated.1` rows containing **full message payloads per update** (measured 0.4 events/s during wait phases, bursts during streaming).
- Unbounded growth: the event table accumulated **273k rows / 2.5 GB** over ~4 weeks of use (84% of the whole database; conversations themselves were only ~320 MB). Cleaning it improved but did not eliminate the lag.

### Ruled out
- **Session size**: new empty session lags the same as a 100+ message session
- **Window size**: few-pixels window lags the same as 2560x1440
- **Database size**: 3 GB → 644 MB (VACUUM) improved agent-time lag but typing lag persists
- **Antivirus**: Avast disabled during tests → identical
- **GPU/driver**: GTX 1060 OK with recent driver; lag also with a tiny render surface
- **System-wide stalls**: Notepad stays perfectly smooth at the same moment
- **Disk space**: 250 GB free

### Suspected mechanism
Per-keystroke work in the renderer (editor re-render / effect re-run per input event — the pattern found in PR #41517), plus unbounded `event` table growth that amplifies lag while the agent streams (full-payload `message.updated` events).

- #37336 — TUI intermittently delays/drops keystrokes (open, same symptom)
- #40225 — v2 composer typing cost scales with draft lines (open)
- #42657 — TUI lag, 97% CPU render thread, 1.18.18 (open)
- #38435 — TUI laggy with large sessions (open)
- #11537, #8484, #23330 — similar input lag, fixed in the past
- PR #41517 — documents per-keystroke effect/focus thrash in inputs

JUST API

Scope addition after further testing: built-in slash commands cannot be removed or shadowed cleanly, and plugin commands cannot safely take a built-in command id.

Concrete case: a TUI plugin registers a command with `slash: { name: "agents" }`. The built-in `agent.list` ("Switch agent") owns that slash name:

- Registering a plugin command with the same id (`agent.list`) is silently dropped — the built-in wins and the plugin command disappears.
- `keybinds: { "agent.list": "none" }` in `cli.json` removes the keybind but the slash entry remains.
- The plugin disable prefix (`-`) applies to plugins, not built-in commands.

Partial workaround found: keymap layers sort by `priority`, so a plugin layer with priority > 0 lists its same-named slash command above the built-in, making it the default selection in autocomplete. But the built-in entry remains visible below, and there is no way to remove it.

Requests: (1) allow plugin commands to override built-in command ids instead of being silently dropped, and/or (2) a config surface to hide built-in slash commands. Would fix this request and general TUI customization.

Following up on the workflow-status example above: I would like to implement a small first slice, subject to the required design review.

Proposed scope:
- Plugins push bounded plain-text title/summary, semantic state, optional progress and detail rows through a host-scoped publisher. OpenCode owns rendering; no HTML, actions, arbitrary components, or chat injection.
- The loader supplies publisher ownership. Revisions are scoped to a plugin generation; disposal invalidates old callbacks.
- Ephemeral server state, a read-only session snapshot endpoint, and typed replacement events with host epoch/sequence ordering. Plugins republish after restart. Removal sends an updated snapshot, including an empty list.
- One compact collapsible surface in the shared Desktop/Web app, hidden when empty. Exact placement is for design review. Existing TUI slots stay unchanged in this first slice.

Tests would cover publisher/session isolation, reload/restart, snapshot/event races, removal, bounded storage/update rates, and Desktop/Web session switching. No metrics history or database migration.

@Brendonovich, does this constrained scope fit the intended direction, and is Desktop/Web-first acceptable? If so, could we agree on the contract and placement before implementation? I will keep the feature PR gated on that approval.
